originalTitle: Is 'Trumpflation' real? Why Wall Street fears this could be a reason for stock market crash
simplifiedContent: There's a concern on Wall Street that something called "Trumpflation" could cause the stock market to crash. This worry is due to inflation (or rising prices) being higher than expected, at 3.3%, and interest rates on government loans (Treasury yields) also going up. This could lead the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates high or even increase them, which might affect the value of stocks. If interest rates go up, it could make it more expensive for companies to borrow money, which could hurt their stock prices. This is a problem because stock prices are currently very high, and any change in interest rates could cause them to drop.

originalTitle: World Bank's IFC, HDFC AMC invest in Molbio Diagnostics' Rs 281 crore IPO anchor round
simplifiedContent: Molbio Diagnostics, a company based in Goa, is planning to raise money by selling stocks to the public, known as an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Before the IPO starts on August 10, the company has already raised Rs 281 crore from some big investors, including the World Bank's IFC and HDFC Mutual Fund. This is called an "anchor round" and it's a good sign that these important investors are supporting the company. The company will try to raise a total of Rs 940 crore from its IPO. Some major brokerages think this is a good investment opportunity and are recommending that people buy the stocks.

originalTitle: Market Trading Guide: Jindal Saw among 2 stock recommendations for Monday
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: some companies in India have recently shared their financial results, and most of them have done as well as or better than people expected. This is making investors feel more positive about certain areas of the market. As a result, some experts are recommending that investors consider buying stocks like Jindal Saw on Monday. This could be a good opportunity for investors to make some money, but it's always important to do your own research before making any decisions. The positive earnings results and sector-specific optimism are key factors to consider when thinking about investing in these stocks.

originalTitle: The stock market is finally rising again—and it’s getting cheaper, too
simplifiedContent: The stock market, which is a place where people buy and sell pieces of companies, is doing well and its value is increasing. In fact, a group of 500 big companies, known as the S&P 500, has seen its value go up by 22% over the past year. Even though the market is going up, the prices of these companies are actually becoming more affordable, which is known as valuations coming down. This is a good thing because it means that investors can buy into the market at a more reasonable price. Overall, the market's growth and decreasing valuations are positive signs for investors.

originalTitle: Upcoming IPOs: Shiprocket IPO, Dhoot Transmission IPO among new issues to open next week; full list here
simplifiedContent: There are some new initial public offerings (IPOs) coming up, which means some companies are going to start selling their shares to the public for the first time. Two of these companies are Shiprocket and Dhoot Transmission, and their IPOs will open between August 10 and 12. This is a chance for regular investors like you to buy shares in these companies. At the same time, shares of eight other companies that recently had their IPOs will start trading on the market for the first time. These IPOs are important because they give investors new opportunities to put their money into different companies and potentially earn returns.

originalTitle: Defence stock Apollo Micro Systems declares Q1 results 2026. Revenue jumps 88% YoY to  ₹251 crore, PAT up 43%
simplifiedContent: Apollo Micro Systems, a company that makes products for the defense industry, just released its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The company's revenue, which is the amount of money it made from selling its products, increased by 88% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹251.3 crore. Its net profit, which is the amount of money it made after paying all its expenses, also increased by 43% to ₹25.2 crore. This means the company is making more money from selling its products and is also keeping more of that money as profit. This is a positive sign for the company's financial health and may be good news for people who have invested in the company.
